subject.title: [Feature]: Feature request: Per-agent isolated browser instances with per-profile proxy support (concurrent execution)

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class per-profile managed-browser proxy config plus per-agent/subagent default browser-profile binding, and what security model should govern proxy credentials, SSRF enforcement, profile selection, inheritance, and concurrency limits?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested feature changes public config/API shape, browser egress, and cookie-bearing browser profile routing, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product and security boundary.

options.title: Approve a gated browser-profile design
options.body: Add the feature only with a documented contract for SecretRef-safe proxy auth, explicit proxy/SSRF trust gates, agent/subagent inheritance rules, profile authorization, launch serialization, and resource limits.

options.title: Split the umbrella into narrower tracks
options.body: Let the broad proxy work continue under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/60035 and the subagent browser ownership work continue under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/85672, keeping this issue as coordination only until maintainers consolidate scope.

options.title: Document current workarounds only
options.body: Decline first-class per-agent/per-profile config for now and document explicit profile selection, browser.extraArgs, remote CDP, node-host, and external browser-lock patterns as supported workarounds.

recommendation.title: Approve a gated browser-profile design
recommendation.body: Add the feature only with a documented contract for SecretRef-safe proxy auth, explicit proxy/SSRF trust gates, agent/subagent inheritance rules, profile authorization, launch serialization, and resource limits.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest semantic history on browser ownership, profile/default behavior, and the bundled browser plugin boundary touched by this decision.
